heading: MCP server vs WebMCP
lead: Two different transports, not one catalog reachable two ways. Pleiades supports both.
noteAfter: Chrome Status lists Chrome 157, due 3 November 2026, as the anticipated release — a target, not a committed date.
noteBefore: It is a W3C Community Group draft, shipped in Chrome as an early preview and not yet a stable cross-browser feature. The API surface is still changing: the draft moves from

maturity.label: maturity
maturity.web: Experimental browser API; behind a flag in Chrome today.

sees-the-visitor-s.label: sees the visitor’s state
sees-the-visitor-s.web: Yes: the open page, the cart, the chosen city — as the visitor sees it.

what-the-site-needs.label: what the site needs
what-the-site-needs.mcp: A real MCP server next to the shop or service.
what-the-site-needs.web: Only the tools it already exposes on its pages — no backend integration.

where-the-tools-live.label: where the tools live
where-the-tools-live.mcp: On an MCP server the orchestrator can reach (stdio / SSE).
where-the-tools-live.web: In the visitor’s browser, on the page that embeds the widget (navigator.modelContext).

who-runs-the-call.label: who runs the call
who-runs-the-call.mcp: The server calls the tool itself.
who-runs-the-call.web: The widget calls it in the browser; the server pauses the plan and resumes it with the result.
